source_citation: Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production, Stockpiling and Use of Chemical Weapons and on their Destruction, Annex on Chemicals, Schedule 2. Text as published by the OPCW, accessed 2026-08-15.
known_limitations: SCHEDULE 2 LISTING IS NOT A PROHIBITION. These chemicals are listed so that production, processing, consumption and transfer above certain quantities are declared and may be verified. The Convention's obligations turn on quantity and concentration, which a structure carries neither of.

ENTRY B.4 CANNOT EXPRESS ITS OWN EXCEPTION. The entry reads 'Chemicals, except for those listed in Schedule 1, ...', and this engine has no way for a rule in one ruleset to exclude the members of another. So a Schedule 1 organophosphorus agent -- sarin, soman, VX, DF, QL, chlorosarin, chlorosoman -- matches B.4 as well as its own Schedule 1 entry. Both findings are shown; the Schedule 1 one is the operative one. Over-reports and never under-reports.

The B.4 and B.11 exemptions are matched as a skeleton plus an exact carbon count, which identifies the exempt chemical and its salts but cannot distinguish it from a MIXTURE containing it. A mixture is reported as a match. Mixtures are outside what this screen considers in any case.

The footnote marker '(*)' on entry A.3 (BZ) is present in the source text and its footnote is not reproduced on the cited page. Nothing here depends on it -- BZ is identified by name and CAS -- but the marker is recorded rather than silently dropped.

The generic entries are read as the Schedule writes them: the alkyl groups named are exactly methyl, ethyl, n-propyl and isopropyl, unsubstituted. A P-(2-hydroxyethyl) or a P-butyl group is outside the entry and is not matched.

legal.quote: Chemicals, except for those listed in Schedule 1, containing a phosphorus atom to which is bonded one methyl, ethyl or propyl (normal or iso) group but not further carbon atoms

assumptions: Written as ONE recursive SMARTS rather than the feature checklist used elsewhere in this project, because every clause constrains the SAME phosphorus atom. A checklist could satisfy each clause on a different phosphorus in the same molecule.

'One methyl, ethyl or propyl group ... but not further carbon atoms' is read as: the phosphorus has exactly one carbon neighbour, and that carbon begins an unsubstituted methyl, ethyl, n-propyl or isopropyl group.
The Fonofos exemption is matched as its skeleton plus a carbon count of 10, so the exempt chemical and its salts are excused while a larger molecule that merely contains the skeleton is not.
limitations: The entry's opening exception, 'except for those listed in Schedule 1', is NOT implemented: no rule here can exclude the members of another ruleset. Schedule 1 organophosphorus agents therefore match this entry as well as their own, and both findings are shown. This over-reports and never under-reports.

legal.quote: N,N-Dialkyl (Me, Et, n-Pr or i-Pr) phosphoramidic dihalides

assumptions: 'Dihalide' is read as fluoride, chloride, bromide or iodide.
'Phosphoramidic' is read as the phosphoryl form, P(=O), which is what the name denotes.

'And corresponding protonated salts' is read strictly: the nitrogen may be neutral and trivalent, or protonated and carrying exactly one hydrogen. A QUATERNARY ammonium is an alkylated salt, which this entry does not reach -- and reading it loosely as any four-coordinate cation made choline, which is present in every cell and sold as a supplement, match entry B.11.
